scope: 0.8B TP1 normal-scheduling performance matrix; no Host-cache reuse observed
findings: All 18 runs passed and ended quiescent; actual device arena and 16 usable device blocks match across modes.
Every run had 16 first-admission prefix misses and zero prefix hits; all on runs had writebacks but no completed H2D loadbacks.
The temporally high-reuse workload did not produce cache reuse with L2 budgets 8 or 16 LCM blocks. These results do not establish an offloading speed benefit.
Off recomputed and completed successfully at the same device budget; no off-mode capacity failure is claimed.
High-reuse extended-phase median paired throughput ratios were 0.972 (L2 ratio0.5) and1.000 (ratio1); low-reuse ratios0.994 and1.002. Small variations are not a statistically established effect.
Host physical destination replacements demonstrate churn but are not a complete logical eviction count.
limits: Instrumented synthetic greedy-token workloads; timing includes observation and replay.
Cold first batch, remaining initial prompts and extended revisits remain separate.
Three sequential fresh Engine repetitions; order is not randomized and shared-server contention may drift.
Prefix hits span all cache tiers; physical Host slot replacements are not all logical eviction events.
Logical Host tensor allocations do not measure physical pinned reserved memory or RSS.
A workload described as high reuse may still miss if both cache budgets are too small.
